references.text: The Israelites already complained to Moses and Aaron because their burdens became heavier, which shows the growing discouragement among the people.
Pharaoh increased the labor burden on the Israelites, leading to the hard service (עֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה) mentioned in our text.
Describes the hard service (עֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה) that the Egyptians imposed on the Israelites, the same expression used in Exodus 6:9.
The people became impatient (קֹצֶר נֶפֶשׁ), a similar expression for shortness of spirit/soul as קֹצֶר רוּחַ in our text.
Job uses the expression קֹצֶר רוּחַ (shortness of spirit) in his complaint, the same expression that describes the Israelites' condition.
Warns against קְצַר־רוּחַ (short of spirit), showing that this is a state of discouragement and impatience.
Stephen's speech refers to how the Egyptians oppressed the ancestors of the Israelites and forced them to expose their children, confirming the harsh treatment.
Stephen quotes God's words that He has seen His people's suffering in Egypt, confirming the context for the Israelites' discouragement.
Highlights the connection between the people's discouragement and God's diagnosis of them as a 'stiff-necked people'.
Fulfillment of prophecy: Exodus 4 predicts that the people will not listen, which occurs in Exodus 6.
Thematic parallel: Both verses illustrate the prophet speaking to a people who refuse to listen or respond.
